heading.en: Can a cricket ball be a wave?

hook.en: If light, a wave, can behave like particles, can particles behave like waves? De Broglie said yes. An electron microscope works only because electrons behave as waves.
hook.kn: ತರಂಗವಾದ ಬೆಳಕು ಕಣದಂತೆ ವರ್ತಿಸಬಹುದಾದರೆ, ಕಣಗಳು ತರಂಗದಂತೆ ವರ್ತಿಸಬಹುದೇ? ಹೌದು ಎಂದರು ಡಿ ಬ್ರೋಗ್ಲಿ. ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಸೂಕ್ಷ್ಮದರ್ಶಕ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುವುದೇ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗಳು ತರಂಗದಂತೆ ವರ್ತಿಸುವುದರಿಂದ.

title.en: Explain why Bohr orbits had to be replaced

say.en: If light, a wave, can behave like particles, can particles behave like waves? De Broglie said yes. An electron microscope works only because electrons behave as waves. In this lesson: Calculate de Broglie wavelengths.
State Heisenberg's uncertainty principle.
Explain why Bohr orbits had to be replaced.

body.en: *De Broglie* (1924) proposed that every moving particle has a wavelength λ = h/mv = h/p. For an electron it is comparable to atomic sizes and shows up in electron diffraction; for a cricket ball it is far too small (≈ 10$^{-34}$ m) to detect. Wave behaviour therefore matters only for microscopic particles.
body.kn: ಡಿ ಬ್ರೋಗ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರಕಾರ ಚಲಿಸುವ ಪ್ರತಿ ಕಣಕ್ಕೂ ತರಂಗಾಂತರ λ = h/mv ಇದೆ. ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗೆ ಇದು ಗಮನಾರ್ಹ; ಕ್ರಿಕೆಟ್ ಚೆಂಡಿಗೆ ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಸಣ್ಣದು.

say.en: Significant only for very small masses.
Basis of the electron microscope.
De Broglie combined Einstein's E equals m c squared with Planck's E equals h c over lambda. For any particle, lambda equals h over m v.

An electron at 10 to the 6 metres per second has a wavelength of about 0.73 nanometre, the size of atoms. A 0.1 kilogram ball at 10 metres per second has a wavelength of 6.6 times 10 to the minus 34 metre: undetectable.
The wavelength falls as the speed rises, as one over v. Here is lambda in nanometres for an electron.
Heisenberg: we cannot know both position and momentum exactly. Pinning an electron to 0.1 nanometre leaves its speed uncertain by about 5.8 times 10 to the 5 metres per second.

say.en: A moving particle has a wavelength lambda equals h over mv. For an electron it is about the size of an atom; for a proton it is far smaller. Squeezing the position spread delta x widens the velocity spread: delta x delta v is greater than or equal to h over 4 pi m.
say.kn: ಚಲಿಸುವ ಕಣಕ್ಕೆ lambda equals h over mv ತರಂಗಾಂತರ. ಇಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ಗೆ ಅದು ಪರಮಾಣು ಗಾತ್ರದಷ್ಟು; ಪ್ರೋಟಾನ್‌ಗೆ ತುಂಬಾ ಚಿಕ್ಕದು. delta x ಕಡಿಮೆ ಮಾಡಿದರೆ delta v ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ: delta x delta v is greater than or equal to h over 4 pi m.

body.en: It is impossible to know both the exact position and the exact momentum of an electron at the same time: $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p_x \ge h/4\pi$. Locating an electron precisely (with short-wavelength light) disturbs its momentum. So a sharply defined Bohr orbit, which needs both, has no meaning for an electron; we can speak only of the probability of finding it in a region.
body.kn: ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್‌ನ ನಿಖರ ಸ್ಥಾನ ಮತ್ತು ನಿಖರ ಸಂವೇಗವನ್ನು ಏಕಕಾಲದಲ್ಲಿ ತಿಳಿಯಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಿಲ್ಲ. ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ನಿಶ್ಚಿತ ಬೋರ್ ಕಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಅರ್ಥವಿಲ್ಲ; ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರಾನ್ ಸಿಗುವ ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆಯನ್ನು ಮಾತ್ರ ಹೇಳಬಹುದು.

steps.en: λ = 6.626 × 10⁻³⁴ m, far too small to observe.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.1 kg ball moving at 10 m s⁻¹.

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the de Broglie wavelength of a 0.1 kilograms ball moving at 10 metres s to the power minus 1.
lambda equals h over mv equals 6.626 times 10 to the power minus 34 / 0.1 times 10.
lambda equals 6.626 times 10 to the power minus 34 metres, far too small to observe.
So the answer is 6.6 times 10 to the power minus 34 metres.

problem.en: An electron (mass 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg) moves at 2.19 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Find its de Broglie wavelength.

steps.en: λ = 3.32 × 10⁻¹⁰ m = 332 pm, comparable to the size of an atom.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. An electron (mass 9.1 × 10⁻³¹ kg) moves at 2.19 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. Find its de Broglie wavelength.

say.en: Let us solve this together. An electron (mass 9.1 times 10 to the power minus 31 kilograms) moves at 2.19 times 10 to the power 6 metres s to the power minus 1. Find its de Broglie wavelength.
lambda equals h over mv equals 6.626 times 10 to the power minus 34 / (9.1 times 10 to the power minus 31 times 2.19 times 10 to the power 6).
lambda equals 3.32 times 10 to the power minus 10 metres equals 332 pm, comparable to the size of an atom.
So the answer is 3.32 times 10 to the power minus 10 metres 332 pm.

lambda is proportional to 1 over v for equal masses; vA equals 2vB, so lambda A: lambda B equals 1: 2.
